Thanks for your PR, here are a few questions wrt your approach/situation:

> This is due to the fact that two job workers concurrently process activeDeadlineSeconds and the other one add a higher value a new item to the queue as seen here:
> [https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L485]

How is that possible that 2 controllers are concurrently processing the same job? Theoretically an object picked from the queue should by one controller should not be synchronously picked by another while the first hasn't finished processing.

/triage accepted
/priority backlog

@soltysh 
EXP: 
1. the controller1 received a new job1, called `SyncJob()`, but it has not called `jm.updateHandler(&job)` to update job status, then job.Status.StartTime is still nil
2. then a job pod was created, enqueued the job1, the controller2 called `SyncJob()` again, this would be the case

Even we are facing a similar issue with cronjobs where some of the CronJobs failed to stop even though "activeDeadlineSeconds" parameter was defined in the template. Any updates on when this issue would be resolved?

@soltysh I have added a testcase to illustrate the suspend job design below(https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-apps/2232-suspend-jobs#design-details):

> If a Job is created with suspend: true, the StartTime field of the Job status is set only when it is resumed for the first time.

If a creation suspend job becomes resume status,  reset the StarTime may still cause ActiveDeadlineSeconds lost efficacy

> If a creation suspend job becomes resume status, reset the StarTime may still cause ActiveDeadlineSeconds lost efficacy

Correct, but that was a conscious decision that we've heavily discussed in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/98727 and then updated the KEP accordingly.

@soltysh This is actually a race condition problem  as two job-workers (goroutines) update job statuses all contains starttime just in time. so inside a worker's sync, we could not know whether another job has just updated the job status with a short early starttime, we only can check this while writing to storage. so I think doing this in updateHandler can be more accurate. But the condition below may not be neccessary, because my target is to prevent starttime set multi-times even though it won't enter that condition at all.
> if job.Status.Active != active || job.Status.Succeeded != succeeded || job.Status.Failed != failed || jobConditionsChanged  || setStartTime {
/cc @soltysh for the new fix, thanks

This pr has stayed for a long time, do you have plan to promote this bug? @kubernetes/sig-apps-pr-reviews

@soltysh Thanks for your review, the case is as follows that i explained before: 
1. the controller1 received a new job1, called SyncJob(), but it has not called jm.updateHandler(&job) to update job status, then job.Status.StartTime is still nil
2. then a job pod was created, enqueued the job1, the controller2 called SyncJob() again, which would set the job.Status.StartTime again, but the delay queue trigger time would not be reset to a later time(see the issue for details)
3.  when the delay queue trigger time comes, the current time which mimus job starttime is still less than the activedeadline, that would be the case
I our environment(which is not have high performance), we can reproduce the bug easily using the job template in the issue, maybe i can add a e2e test case for test coverage  to prevent regression

issue_context.title: Job didn't delete pods within activeDeadlineSeconds
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

Currently, sometimes, while create nums of jobs with **spec.activeDeadlineSeconds** concurrently, some job may not terminate it's pod while exceed activeDeadlineSeconds

1. the jobs template

```
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: testjob
spec:
  activeDeadlineSeconds: 60
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: testjob
        image: tutum/curl
        command:
          - sleep
          - "360000"
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
      restartPolicy: Never

 .................................

kind: Job
metadata:
  name: testjob9
spec:
```

I agree that there is a bug, but I disagree with the analysis.

> This is due to the fact that two job workers concurrently process activeDeadlineSeconds and the other one add a higher value a new item to the queue

What makes you think that two workers were syncing a job concurrently? This shouldn't happen.

In general, any immediate sync would clear a future "AddAfter". So the bug here is that we are only setting AddAfter once, instead of every time there is a sync.

the debug log, testjob8 ActiveDeadlineSeconds triggered twice, jobStatus.startTime was re-set to 16:55:50.242498（to UTC time， minus 8，08:55:50.242498 ）

1. the controller1 received a new job1, called SyncJob(), but it has not called jm.updateHandler(&job) to update job status, then job.Status.StartTime is still nil
2. then a job pod was created, enqueued the job1, the controller2 called SyncJob() again, which would set the job.Status.StartTime again, but the delay queue trigger time would not be reset to a later time(see the issue for details)
3. when the delay queue trigger time comes, the current time which mimus job starttime is still less than the activedeadline, that would be the case
which version of kubernetes are you running?
In any case, the suggested solution is to `AddAfter` in every sync.
I can reproduce this in v1.19 and v1.22, but recently I could not reproduce in v1.23.x, so I closed this

In 1.21, we introduced this fix #100553, that could potentially reduce uncertainty.

But if you still observed the problem in 1.22, then there is still probably a bug. I propose this solution https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/97101#issuecomment-1115061840

That's a weird problem. I do believe #97101 solves the `StartTime` reset in a very short time, but I don't think it will cause the job doesn't terminate, even if the termination time will be delayed a very short time. Because when the job is resynced, the controller will AddAfter again with the delta duration.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b74d023e70d6064c7f3f77031e7d26ec38497fc9/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L419-L435

For example, after we create a job:
1. controller get the job, find `StartTime` is nil, so set to current time (assuming time is `N`), AddAfter `60s`, create pods, update job status
2. because of pod creation event, controller get the job again, the job from Informer has not updated to the latest status, so controller find `StartTime` is nil, set to current time (assuming time is `N+300ms`), AddAfter `60s` (but workqueue will just keep the delaying event added previously), update job status
3. 60s after `N`, the job is triggered again. controller find it has not reach the expected deadline, which is actually `N+300ms+60s`, so it will AddAfter the job with `300ms`
4. 300ms after, the job will be triggered and controller should terminate it.

So, IMHO, the bug that #97101 aims to fix, might cause the start and termination time delaying in a very short time, but it should not delay a few seconds or more like the issue log shows, **unless the job informer had not been updated for a long time**.
